Subject: Post-demo: prompt collection & model-fit next steps

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Recap: we walked through Redwood Inference hosted inference and Dedicated options, discussed your main goals (latency budgets for customer-facing chat, cost targets at 50k qps equivalent, and strict data redaction for support transcripts).
- Ask: to run an initial model-fit evaluation, could you share a representative prompt set and any edge-case examples you’re worried about (PII, legal disclaimers, multi-turn context with long histories)?
- Template: attaching a small prompt-collection template that teams usually fill out (categories, expected outputs, redaction flag). That helps our eval team prioritize.
- Timeline: if you can send samples by end of next week (7/23) we can return an initial eval with recommended models and benchmark links within 5 business days.

Notes on redaction: please mark any prompt rows that contain PII or PHI in the template, and include an anonymized version if possible. If you need guidance on safe redaction, we can provide examples (we're strict about never ingesting raw PHI into hosted evals without a contract).

Next steps:
1) Emily — upload prompt samples (or reply with files).
2) Rishi — run initial model-fit and propose 2-3 candidate models + quantization profile.
3) I'll follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-minute review.

Attaching: prompt_collection_template.csv (blank template).

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

Best,

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. Attaching an initial export of prompts our support team has anonymized (acme_prompt_samples.csv). We tried to scrub obvious customer identifiers, but we have two specific questions: 

1) We do have occasional legal/contract snippets in prompts — should we fully redact or provide a tokenized placeholder (e.g., [CONTRACT_TEXT])?
2) We need recommended models that can handle multi-turn context up to ~2k tokens and preserve slot values across turns. Latency target is 300ms p95 for short responses.

Also attaching a short sample of edge cases we’ve seen in prod. If you need production logs rather than samples, we can coordinate with our security team (let me know what evidence you need).

Thanks — happy to schedule the follow-up once you’ve reviewed.

—Emily

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: prompt collection & model-fit next steps

Emily — appreciate the samples. A few quick recommendations based on a preliminary look: 

- Models: for your latency target and ~2k token context we recommend starting with two candidates:
  1) rw-large-arch-v2 (fp16) — best quality for multi-turn retention; expect higher token cost but better slot/value preservation.
  2) rw-latency-8q (8-bit quantized) — trades some long-tail quality for ~2x cost savings and lower latency; good for scaling.

- Benchmarks: I’ve kicked off a run against the sample set and uploaded preliminary results here: https://redwood.inference/benchmarks/acme-model-fit (contains p95/p50 latency, token cost, and accuracy on your labeled set).

- Prompt handling / redaction: provide both raw (if allowed under your security policy) and a redacted copy. If raw cannot be shared, use token placeholders for lengthy contract snippets — we can still run contextual tests if you mark placeholders and provide one or two full examples in a secure channel (we can do an on-prem eval or use a Private deployment trial).

- Edge cases: please capture examples that cause hallucination or context loss across turns; mark expected vs. unacceptable outputs in the template. That helps our evaluation scripts flag regressions.

Attachment: model_recommendation_acme.pdf (detailed notes + recommended quant profiles).

I’ll follow up with a short eval summary and specific run IDs once the full sample set is in. If you’d like, we can include a regression alert baseline tied to your prompt set to catch quality drift after rollout.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
